description: Phase 9: DevOps. Create multi-stage Dockerfile with non-root user, docker-compose.yml with nginx/web (gunicorn)/postgres services, GitHub Actions CI workflow for ruff lint and tests with coverage, management command seed_demo to create realistic demo data for all 3 roles, comprehensive README.md with setup/features/architecture, and docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md with Mermaid diagrams for entity relationships, request flow, and deployment architecture.
steps: 1. Create Dockerfile in project root: multi-stage build with base stage (Python 3.12, dependencies), builder stage (copy code), final stage (non-root user 'appuser', COPY from builder, EXPOSE 8000, CMD gunicorn). Use requirements/prod.txt.
2. Create .dockerignore with patterns: venv/, __pycache__/, *.pyc, db.sqlite3, .env, .git/, htmlcov/, .coverage, logs/

3. Create docker-compose.yml with services: db (postgres:16-alpine, environment POSTGRES_DB/USER/PASSWORD, volume for data), web (build: ., depends_on: db, environment DATABASE_URL/SECRET_KEY/ALLOWED_HOSTS/JOB_MODERATION_ENABLED, volumes for media/private/static, command gunicorn), nginx (nginx:alpine, depends_on: web, ports 80:80, volumes for static/media, config)
4. Create nginx/nginx.conf with upstream to web:8000, location / proxy_pass, location /static/ and /media/ serve files

5. Create .github/workflows/ci.yml: name 'CI', on push/pull_request to main, jobs: lint (ruff check .), test (setup Python 3.12, install requirements/dev.txt, run tests, coverage, upload coverage report as artifact)

6. Create management command core/management/commands/seed_demo.py: Clear existing data (optional flag --clear), create 3 users (job seeker, recruiter, admin) with known passwords (in output), create 2 verified companies (1 for recruiter), create 5 categories, 15 skills, create 10 jobs (varied categories, skills, locations, job types, some expired), create 3 job seeker profiles with education/experience/resumes (mock files), create 15 applications (varied statuses), create 5 interviews, create job alerts, create notifications, create job reports, create contact messages, create audit logs. Output summary of created data.
7. Update requirements/base.txt to include 'faker' for seed_demo realistic data generation

8. Create README.md in project root with sections: Project Title & Description, Features (bullet list covering all phases), Tech Stack (Django 5.1.3, PostgreSQL, Bootstrap 5.3, Chart.js, gunicorn, nginx, Docker), Prerequisites, Setup Instructions (local: clone, venv, install requirements/dev.txt, copy .env.example, migrate, createsuperuser, runserver; Docker: docker-compose up --build), Demo Data (python manage.py seed_demo), Running Tests (python manage.py test, coverage), Project Structure (tree or description), Key Features by Role (job seeker, recruiter, admin), Contributing, License
9. Create .env.example with all required environment variables: SECRET_KEY, DEBUG, ALLOWED_HOSTS, DATABASE_URL, EMAIL_*, JOB_MODERATION_ENABLED, MAX_RESUME_SIZE_MB, etc.

11. Create docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md with sections: Overview, Architecture Overview, Entity Relationship Diagram (Mermaid), Database Schema (tables and relationships), Request Flow Diagram (Mermaid: user -> nginx -> gunicorn -> Django -> PostgreSQL), Component Diagram (Mermaid: apps and dependencies), Deployment Architecture (Mermaid: Docker containers, nginx, web, db), Key Design Decisions (split settings, services pattern, private file storage, signal-based notifications, moderation toggle), Security Considerations (email verification, password validation, django-axes, SECURE_* settings, permission checks), Performance Optimizations (indexes, query optimization, WhiteNoise for static files), Future Enhancements (payment integration, real-time chat, video interviews, AI resume parsing)
12. Create Mermaid ER diagram in SYSTEM_DESIGN.md showing User, Company, Job, Application, Notification, JobAlert, Interview, etc. with relationships

13. Create Mermaid sequence diagram in SYSTEM_DESIGN.md showing typical application flow: Job Seeker applies -> Application created -> Signal -> Notification sent -> Recruiter reviews -> Status changed -> Signal -> Email sent
14. Create Mermaid deployment diagram showing Docker setup: nginx container, gunicorn container, postgres container, volume mounts
18. Test CI workflow by creating a test branch and pushing (or simulate locally with ruff and pytest)
acceptance_criteria: Dockerfile builds successfully with multi-stage build, runs as non-root user 'appuser'
docker-compose.yml orchestrates nginx, web (gunicorn), postgres services with proper networking and volumes
nginx.conf proxies requests to gunicorn and serves static/media files
GitHub Actions CI workflow runs on push/PR, executes ruff lint and tests with coverage
.github/workflows/ci.yml uses Python 3.12, installs dev requirements, runs tests, generates coverage report

Management command seed_demo creates realistic demo data: 3 users (job seeker, recruiter, admin), 2 companies, 10 jobs, 3 profiles with education/experience, 15 applications, 5 interviews, job alerts, notifications, reports
seed_demo outputs summary with usernames and passwords for easy login
README.md includes comprehensive setup instructions, feature list, tech stack, project structure
.env.example lists all required environment variables with example values
docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md includes Mermaid diagrams: ER diagram (entities and relationships), sequence diagram (application flow), deployment diagram (Docker architecture)
All diagrams render correctly in Markdown viewers (GitHub, VS Code)
docker-compose up successfully runs the application accessible at localhost:80
CI workflow passes on push (linting and tests succeed)
verification: Run: docker build -t hirehub . (from project root)
Verify demo data created, note output usernames/passwords
Login with seeded accounts (job seeker, recruiter, admin), verify data present
Verify no linting errors (or fix them)
Push to GitHub (or simulate CI locally), verify workflow runs and passes
Open docs/SYSTEM_DESIGN.md in GitHub or VS Code, verify Mermaid diagrams render
Review README.md for completeness and accuracy
